newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* Edmund Jenkins, the former managing director of Arthur Andersen, has been named the new chairman of the Financial Accounting Standards Board, sources said.

* Eli Lilly said it would take a charge of $4.40 per share in the second quarter to write down the carrying value of its PCS health care management business, ackowleding it paid too much for the unit in 1994.
* Union Pacific Resources launched an unsolicited multibillion-dollar bid for Pennzoil, a petroleum company that said it would review the offer.
* British-Dutch publisher, Reed-Elsevier, has agreed to acquire Walt Disney Co's Chilton trade magazine group for $447 million.
* Alcatel Alsthom and Cisco Systems formed a strategic partnership to develop equipment using current and new technologies to integrate the Internet with telephone networks.
* Paxson Communications Corp has agreed to sell its radio holdings to Clear Channel Communications for $693 million in cash.

* Fox/Liberty Networks, a joint venture of News Corp's Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp, has agreed to invest $850 million for a 40 percent stake in Rainbow Media Holdings Inc's sports interests.

* Prices of Treasury securities fell late in the day amid remarks by Japan Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that worried U.S. financial markets about his call for U.S.-Japan foreign exchange cooperation.
* Toy Biz now has two boards of directors as a result of a battle with Marvel Entertainment Group Inc, which owns about 25 percent of Toy Biz.
* The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that employees of private companies that run prisons under contract are not entitled to the same immunity from prisoner lawsuits enjoyed by public prison guards.
* Cigarette makers may have been hampered in their marketing efforts in the U.S. from the recent tobacco settlement, but they may have other frontiers: Eastern Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
* Compaq Computer has agreed to acquire Tandem Computers for about $3 billion in a stock swap.
* Microsoft founder Bill Gates has created a foundation that intends to spend $200 million over five years to bring computers and the Internet to public libraries in the United States.
* The Dow Jones Industrials dropped 192.25 points on Monday, closing at 7604.26, posting its worst day in 1997.

* Thomas Donohue, the new president of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, is a pit bull of lobbying, who knows his way around Washington and is likely to bring a "new edge" to the country's leading business lobby.
